business.description: Lokesh Machines Limited manufactures CNC machine tools, special purpose machines (SPMs), general purpose machines (GPMs), precision auto components, forgings, and indigenously developed small arms. The company serves automotive OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers, and the Indian Armed Forces from six manufacturing units in Hyderabad and Pune.

outlook.statement: Expect trajectory to continue as customer relationships and international operations normalise; focus on deepening engagement with Ministry of Defence, Defence PSUs and private aerospace manufacturers; rebuilding export markets; product development in high-speed, multi-axis CNC machines; working-capital discipline for steady, sustainable returns.

Expect demand for CNC machine tools and precision manufacturing solutions to keep supporting order book in years ahead, driven by automation/Industry 4.0 adoption, import substitution push, and indigenous defence production.
The Company expects operating cash flow to unwind as blocked channels reopen and stock converts to dispatches following OFAC delisting effective 30 June 2026.
EV drive-train and battery structural components viewed as a growth area for both Auto Component and Machine Tools divisions.

Indian machine tool industry continues to expand on the back of PLI schemes, Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence, and capacity investment across automotive, general engineering, railways and heavy engineering.

Near-term outlook shaped by restoration of international banking channels and resumption of business with counterparties that curtailed dealings during OFAC designation; continued order intake in Machine Tools division from non-automotive clusters; growth in Defence division supported by DGQA registration, HMG licensing recommendation and CAPF/Armed Forces tenders; and diversification of Auto Component customer base alongside entry into forgings and EV components.

Principal challenges are pace of normalisation of banking and counterparty relationships (may take several quarters, not entirely within Company's control); continued dependence on automotive capital-expenditure cycle for a portion of revenue; and execution risk in scaling Defence division pending tender outcomes.
Auto Component relationship with principal customer restored from FY27; order book conversion to dispatches expected; workforce planning to track recovery pace

R&D priorities: commercialisation of newly productionised machines; launch of H650 Horizontal Machining Centre, VTL-1250 Ram-type CNC Vertical Turning Lathe, Double Column Plano Miller; continued development of new weapon platforms
Shortage of skilled CNC programmers, mechatronics engineers and defence-tooling technicians remains a constraint on scaling capacity

Commercialization of above new products. Launch of Bigger size Horizontal Machining Centers - H650. Launch of CNC Vertical Turning Lathe (Ram type) - VTL-1250. Launch of Double column Plano Miller. Developing new weapon platforms.

The Company also undertook renewed strategic initiatives to recoup its business, which have yielded positive outcomes, evidenced by the emergence of new business opportunities and the onboarding of new customers.

orders_or_contracts.statement: Order book grew from ₹59.4 crore (31 Mar 2025) to ₹147.2 crore (31 Mar 2026), up 147.8%; further to ₹271 crore (12 Aug 2026), up 84.1% in just over four months.
Delivery of indigenous small arms to Indian Army and special forces, an Indian first for a private-sector company.
Executed development and commercial supply orders for EV drive-train and battery structural components during FY26.

Order book as of 12 August 2026 stood at ₹271.00 crore, significantly exceeding the whole of the previous financial year's revenue and providing multi-quarter visibility over and above the first quarter's billings.
Defence order inflows included an order of ₹58.21 crore received on 15 July 2026 from the Ministry of Defence (Army) for 7.62 mm medium machine gun upgradation kits.
